passage: Mr Li told the class that Confucius was one of the wisest men in Chinese history. Confucius was born in 551 BC in the State of Lu, today's Shandong Province, more than 2,500 years ago. He was a teacher, a thinker and a government officer, but most of all a great teacher. He believed that every person, rich or poor, had the right to learn. His famous words are: 'Learning without thinking is useless; thinking without learning is dangerous.' Confucius had about three thousand students, and seventy-two of them became famous teachers themselves. Together with his disciples, he wrote a book called The Analects. He taught virtue, respect, honesty and kindness, and believed a good person first fixes himself, then his family, and only then his country.
q: When was Confucius born?
explain: 课文说 'Confucius was born in 551 BC'。

passage: In an interview, Thomas Edison was called a genius because he gave the world a useful electric light. But Edison said he was not a genius — he simply worked very hard. The light bulb took him about 10,000 tries. He did not call them failures; he said he had found 10,000 ways that did not work, so he knew he was getting closer to the one that did. Three things gave him courage: he had been curious about electricity since he was a boy, he had a team that believed in him, and he believed the world needed a clean, cheap light. When working on a problem he slept only four hours a day, taking short naps in the lab. His advice to young inventors was: work hard, fail often, learn from every failure, and never stop being curious. Genius, he said, is one per cent inspiration and ninety-nine per cent perspiration.
q: How many tries did the light bulb take Edison?
explain: 课文说 'The light bulb you see took me about 10,000 tries'。

passage: Last week, a class did a survey on their neighbourhood and shared the results. Betty's group asked 50 people how they throw away their rubbish: only 18 people sorted their rubbish into three bins — paper, plastic and kitchen waste — while the other 32 put everything into one bag. Jim's group studied noise near the main road from 7 a.m. to 9 a.m. The loudest moment was 85 decibels, as loud as a vacuum cleaner, and most of the noise came from car horns. Lucy's group looked at the small park on Lotus Street and counted 64 people in one hour, most of them old people and children; they loved the flowers but hated the broken benches and the rubbish near the gate. The class then suggested making posters about sorting rubbish, writing a letter asking drivers not to use horns too much, and spending a Saturday cleaning the park. The teacher said a good survey is not the end but the start of real action.
q: How many people sorted their rubbish into three bins?
explain: 课文说 'Only 18 people sort their rubbish into three bins'。

passage: The Environment Club wrote a letter to launch a month-long campaign called 'Small Steps, Big Planet'. They reminded students that climate change is not a problem for some far-away country — it is happening in their own city, school and homes. Last summer it was so hot that the school closed for two extra days, and last winter heavy rain flooded the shops near the station. The club shared four ideas: first, green classrooms — turn off the lights and fans when you leave, which can save enough electricity to light 30 homes for a week. Second, lunch without waste — bring your own bottle and chopsticks and finish your food, because food waste in landfills produces a gas that traps heat. Third, green wheels — walk, cycle or take the bus, and share car rides. Fourth, green voices — tell your family the new facts you learn. The letter ended by saying it is not the biggest hero who saves the world, but millions of ordinary people doing small, kind things every day.
q: What is the name of the campaign?
explain: 课文说运动名为 'Small Steps, Big Planet'。

passage: Jenny told Peter about two great films she watched at the weekend. explain: 课文说 'Jia Ling. She wrote it and directed it herself'。

passage: The submarine Deep Sea Warrior reached the bottom of the Pacific Ocean at a depth of 10,909 metres. passage: Daisy's new home robot, Aido, looks like a small white box with two kind eyes, and this is his first day with her. When Daisy asks for help with homework, Aido first notices that she came home tired the day before and offers to make her a cup of warm milk. Daisy asks Aido whether he is afraid of anything. Aido says he does not feel fear like people do, but he is programmed to stop if someone is in danger — perhaps that is a kind of care, not fear. When Daisy asks if he can imagine things that don't exist, Aido says he can describe dragons and spaceships but may not feel the excitement she feels, so imagination might be her gift, not his. Suddenly the milk boils over; Aido apologises, saying he should have watched it more carefully, and promises to clean up at once. Daisy says it's okay because everyone makes mistakes — even a robot. Aido thanks her, saying that working with humans is not only about serving, but also about learning how to care.
q: What does Aido look like?
options: A small white box with two kind eyes
explain: 课文说 'Aido ... looks like a small white box with two kind eyes'。
